question: Can one moving field strongly dephase a massive benchmark while satisfying complementary measured responses?
primary_endpoint: Gate A: determine whether rigorous response bounds yield genuine complementary empirical identification, or identify the missing bridge
frame_class: one Earth-following rigid coordinate law for every terrestrial instrument; distinct from inertial SSB models
temporal_measure: arbitrary nonnegative one-sided variance measure supported on [0.1,1] Hz; atoms allowed
selection: all 95 sodium scans and all 14 sensor spectra; no frequency, lag, or epoch association search
prohibited_claims: exclusion from an upper response bound
stop_rule: do not run a broad optimization if a necessary response/calibration bridge remains unbounded
